question.prompt:
The diagram below shows the circular face of a clock with radius \(20\) cm and a circular disk with radius \(10\) cm externally tangent to the clock face at \(12\) o’clock. The disk has an arrow painted on it, initially pointing in the upward vertical direction. Let the disk roll clockwise around the clock face. At what point on the clock face will the disk be tangent when the arrow is next pointing in the upward vertical direction?

[Figure 1](figures/2015_AMC_10A_Q14_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Interpret rolling as rolling without slipping. Track both the disk's turn relative to the line joining the two centers and the turn of that line itself.

Let \(\theta\) be the clockwise angle, in degrees, that the contact point has moved around the clock from 12 o'clock. The line joining the centers also turns clockwise by \(\theta\) degrees. Let \(\psi\) be the disk's clockwise turn measured relative to that moving line. Measuring this way keeps the disk's contact radius in a fixed direction, so \(\psi\) measures the disk rim that has passed through contact.

Without slipping, equal lengths of the two rims pass through contact. Consequently,
\[
\frac{\theta}{360}(2\pi\cdot20)
=\frac{\psi}{360}(2\pi\cdot10),
\]
which gives \(\psi=2\theta\).

Both turns are clockwise. Adding the disk's relative turn to the turn of the line joining the centers, the arrow has turned
\[
\psi+\theta=3\theta
\]
degrees relative to its original upward direction.

As \(\theta\) increases, the arrow's clockwise turn increases. Its first later upward direction therefore occurs after one full turn:
\[
3\theta=360,\qquad \theta=120.
\]
The clock's twelve hour marks are \(360/12=30\) degrees apart. Thus the contact point moves \(120/30=4\) hour marks clockwise from 12, reaching \(\boxed{4\text{ o'clock}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Match contact arcs and combine the turns
Match contact arcs and include the moving frame turn
